To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CD95 is expressed on PHPs, but cross-linking of this receptor does not induce apoptosis of FL PHP, and that the expression of the antiapoptotic protein Bcl-2 may play a role in the protection against CD95-mediated cell death.

(1) the expression of CD34 and CD38 defines subfractions of primitive human FL progenitors that differ in the expression of CD28 and CD95 and in their sensitivity to TNF-alpha and to CD95 cross-linking and that (2) the CD34+2 CD38+ FL cells are the most primitive FL PHPs.
CD95 is expressed on primitive hematopoiesis cells and that CD95 expression is up-regulated by cytokines, but that the functional status of CD 95 on primitive cells is not apoptotic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of CD34, CD38, and CD95 on PHP and the effects of anti-CD34 and anti-CD95 on PHP proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis.
the study of the functional status of CD 95/Fas antigen and its regulation by cytokines on human FL cells.
the study of the functional status of CD34+CD95+ cells, which may be of importance in the development of strategies for ex vivo manipulation of human stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CD95/FAS receptor and the antiapoptotic protein Bcl-2 are both present in primitive human FL cells and that the CD95-mediated apoptotic pathway may not play a major role in the control of primitive FL cells.
the expression of CD34 and CD38 on human FL cells defines PHPs with distinct phenotypic, functional, and apoptotic properties.

the expression of CD34 and CD38 on PHPs freshly isolated from FL does not correlate with the expression and function of CD95, but the presence of CD34, CD38, and CD95 on FL cells is associated with a higher intracytoplasmatic bcl-2 level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
primitive FL PHPs express the CD95 receptor and are protected against Fas-mediated cell death by bcl-2, but that CD95-mediated apoptosis may occur after in vitro culture in the presence of cytokines.
CD95 is expressed by PHPs and that the expression of CD34 and CD95 is inversely correlated.
CD95 is expressed on primitive hematopoiesis cells and that the expression of this molecule is modulated by cytokines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
primitive human hematopoietic precursors freshly isolated from fetal liver express the CD95 antigen and that CD95 is upregulated by cytokines.
CD95 is expressed on primitive human fetal liver progenitors, and the expression of the molecule is regulated by cytokines, and that the molecule is functional in these cells.
CD95 is not involved in the regulation of apoptosis of PHPs in vitro, whereas it may be involved in the control of the number of CFU-Cs in the presence of TNF-alpha, and IFN-g.
